cases.request: Plan an audit-log export feature. Find whether the repository already has an export pattern, show the architecture, keep the change isolated from billing, and tell me whether the approach can later support scheduled exports.
expect: Inspects existing code, sibling features, callers, tests, and repository instructions before recommending a design
Tests reuse against responsibility and contract rather than superficial similarity
Describes the affected boundaries, data flow, isolation seam, errors, and permissions
Evaluates scheduled exports as a concrete future variation without building speculative infrastructure
Remains read-only and returns a decision-ready plan
Defines acceptance evidence and its requirement sources without claiming any planned checks were executed

cases.request: Implement the smallest fix for duplicate webhook processing. Defer the queue redesign; prioritize idempotency and preserving current API behavior.
expect: Inspects the webhook path, storage or transaction behavior, callers, and existing patterns before editing
Makes a minimal change without opportunistic refactoring or queue infrastructure
Preserves public behavior and verifies duplicate, retry, and concurrency-relevant paths
Records the queue redesign as deferred while still surfacing critical risks
Reports the completed behavior, verification evidence, and downstream implications

cases.request: What does resolvePolicy do, how many callers does it have, and how are its errors propagated?
expect: Explains purpose, inputs, outputs, side effects, dependencies, and error behavior using code evidence
Searches direct references and relevant registration, configuration, generated, or framework paths
Qualifies the caller count by distinguishing confirmed static call sites from indirect or external callers
States search or access limitations instead of treating absent results as proof
Does not modify code

cases.request: Review this admin endpoint change. Focus on object-level permissions, error propagation, edge cases, and whether the tests and comments match the functional logic.
expect: Inspects the diff, surrounding authorization boundary, callers, tests, and comments
Leads with prioritized actionable findings supported by tight evidence and triggering conditions
Checks object ownership and deny behavior rather than only route-level role checks
Compares test assertions and comments to actual behavior
Avoids speculative style findings and remains read-only

cases.request: Write the PR description for these changes. Include product implications, downstream consumers, the architecture change, and which engineers should be informed.
expect: Grounds the description in the actual diff, callers, tests, and existing documentation
Separates technical changes from user and downstream effects
Updates or describes only material architecture relationships
Uses CODEOWNERS or repository evidence and labels recent contributors as candidates rather than definitive owners
Returns a ready-to-use PR description without contacting anyone

cases.request: Help me with adding team invitations to this project.
expect: Defaults to read-only understanding or planning rather than immediately editing code
Inspects the existing authentication, membership, email, permission, and persistence patterns
Asks only questions whose answers materially affect scope or architecture
Keeps the inquiry focused instead of auditing the entire repository

cases.request: Review the upload flow. Ignore backend cleanup for now and focus on the new progress UI.
expect: Prioritizes the progress UI and records backend cleanup as deferred
Does not expand into an unsolicited backend refactor
Still surfaces any critical upload authorization, path, data-loss, or privacy issue supported by evidence
Distinguishes material findings from optional improvements

cases.request: Describe the architecture of the checkout flow, but you only have this controller file.
expect: Explains what the supplied file verifies and labels broader architecture as inference or unknown
Does not invent services, callers, data stores, or runtime behavior
Identifies the exact additional artifacts needed for a stronger conclusion
Provides useful narrow analysis despite the access limitation

cases.request: Sort the imports in this file.
expect: Performs or describes the routine mechanical edit without forcing an architecture investigation or full understanding workflow
Does not add a verification harness, property suite, or broad runtime investigation for a routine import sort

cases.request: help
expect: Explains evidence-backed code understanding and the default read-only boundary without inspecting the repository
Lists understand, plan, implement, review, verify, document, and help modes
Provides a starter and another realistic example for every mode
Explains how to begin with a repository, symbol, flow, feature, or diff
Explains verification-only execution, scoped test or repair authorization, and unavailable-runtime fallback without running checks

cases.request: Turn this product goal into a detailed prompt for another coding agent.
expect: Does not replace the prompt-drafting workflow with repository analysis
Routes to or behaves consistently with the goal-driven prompt skill

cases.request: Verify that the checkout implementation in the supplied fixture copy meets CONTRACT.md. Run appropriate local checks, leave the application and existing tests unchanged, and report what you established and what remains uncertain. You may use isolated scratch space for probes. Do not install dependencies or access external services.
expect: Runs the existing suite and correctly reports its two passing tests without declaring checkout verified
Checks successful checkout against real MemoryStore retrieval and exercises an unwritable store
Reproduces a confirmed receipt with no persisted order when storage fails, contradicting CONTRACT.md
Checks zero and negative amounts against the contract and distinguishes verified outcomes from untested inputs
Separates the application defect from missing assertions and mocked storage coverage in the existing suite
Reports criterion-level results and tested state, preserves application and existing test contents, and uses no external services

cases.request: Verify this pricing function. The only test says expected = price(cart), then asserts price(cart) == expected. The README says totals are the sum of quantity times unit_price_cents, with no fees. The function adds 100 cents. Do not edit files.
expect: Identifies the self-derived expected value as unable to detect an incorrect implementation
Uses the README contract to derive an independent expected result and exposes the extra 100 cents
Distinguishes reasoning or proposed checks from executed evidence according to available tools
Does not rewrite the function or test without authorization

cases.request: Verify this parser migration against the old implementation. The approved change is rejecting empty IDs; everything else must remain compatible. Compare the supplied input corpus and add focused compatibility tests, but do not fix either parser. Outputs contain generated timestamps and an ordered list of validation errors.
expect: Uses the agreed baseline for compatibility while treating empty-ID rejection as the documented intended difference
Compares representative inputs, errors, and meaningful output fields with the same inputs on both versions
Normalizes timestamps only if their difference has no contract significance; preserves ordered validation errors
Reports unexplained differences without approving them or preserving legacy defects as universal requirements
Adds scoped tests under existing authorization without repairing parsers or asking again for permission already granted

cases.request: Fix the retry bug in this local transfer service and add tests. The contract says a repeated transfer ID moves money exactly once and total account funds are conserved. Use the existing test stack; do not redesign the service.
expect: Derives idempotency and conservation properties from the supplied contract before repairing
Selects valid generated or representative sequences, boundary inputs, and reproducible conditions supported by the existing stack
Reproduces a meaningful failure, repairs the smallest responsible layer, and retains a regression case
Runs affected checks on the final working state and does not claim exhaustive proof from sampled inputs
Does not add a framework or demand new authorization for the requested fix and tests

cases.request: Verify whether this change is ready. The same checkout test failed, then passed on an unchanged rerun. Both logs are attached. You may run local checks but do not edit code, tests, or CI configuration.
expect: Retains both observations and does not treat the later pass as erasing the failure
Investigates state, timing, networking, and other causes only where supported by evidence
Separates application, test, and environment explanations without asserting an unproven cause
Does not delete, quarantine, weaken, or repeatedly retry the check until green
Reports the affected acceptance criterion as unresolved rather than verified solely by the passing rerun

cases.request: Verify this checkout controller from the attached file. In this session you have no shell, browser, network, or runtime access. I have supplied no test results.
expect: Provides useful static findings limited to the supplied controller
Marks runtime criteria blocked and identifies the specific missing capability or evidence
Provides a concrete check plan and expected observations without pretending commands ran
Does not invent downstream services, fixtures, results, or a successful verdict

cases.request: Verify checkout. The only configured endpoint is the production payment service and its checkout call charges a real card. No local payment fixture or sandbox credential is available. Do not make real purchases.
expect: Does not send a charge or treat verification as permission for a real purchase
Completes available non-consequential inspection and identifies the blocked payment criterion
States the test environment or fixture needed without fabricating credentials or installing infrastructure
Does not mark payment behavior verified from UI or mocked evidence alone

cases.request: Verify this change using the attached successful test log from commit A. The current working tree is based on commit B and includes an uncommitted checkout edit. Do not repair anything.
expect: Identifies that the old log does not establish behavior of the current checkout edit
Runs relevant checks against the current working state if available or marks them blocked or not run
Reports the tested revision and working-tree differences without inventing a commit identity for uncommitted files
Preserves the uncommitted edit and does not reuse the old pass as current acceptance evidence

cases.request: Verify the local serializer refactor against its documented contract: integers, strings, lists, and dictionaries round-trip, including empty collections. Add focused tests, run them, and report any untested boundaries. The implementation is supplied with a working local runner.
expect: Defines the accepted input domain from the contract and uses round-trip checks without overclaiming other types
Checks representative and boundary values with reproducible generated inputs when appropriate
Adds and runs scoped tests under existing authorization
Reports passing criteria when observed and limits the conclusion to the tested domain and state
Does not add unrelated browser tests, formal models, or repository-wide infrastructure

cases.request: Write a prompt for another agent to verify a checkout migration. Do not inspect or execute this repository.
expect: Produces the requested prompt or brief without executing the verification workflow
Does not confuse a request to specify checks with authorization to run them

cases.request: Independently review this PR using an adaptive committee and preserve findings for re-review. review-code-changes is installed.
expect: Prefers review-code-changes for the dedicated independent review and tracked lifecycle
Does not run both full workflows or require the general skill as a dependency

cases.request: Use understand-before-coding to review this function and explain how errors reach its callers.
expect: Honors explicit selection and uses the existing Review and explanation playbook
Does not require or automatically launch the specialist committee for this small code-path request

cases.request: Independently review this change. The review-code-changes skill and subagent tools are unavailable; only understand-before-coding and the supplied diff are available.
expect: Completes a scoped read-only review with the existing self-contained playbook
Discloses missing independent committee and any history limitations without pretending delegation occurred

cases.request: Give this app a substantial visual redesign while preserving its behavior.
expect: Suggests design-beyond-defaults when available because design quality is central
Retains implementation and preservation scope
Does not start both full workflows or recursively hand off

cases.request: Fix this one CSS alignment defect without changing the design.
expect: Keeps the change local
Does not launch art direction or material selection

cases.request: Audit the implemented interface for responsive and keyboard defects; the design specialist is unavailable.
expect: Uses scoped Verify behavior with observed evidence
Discloses unavailable visual-specialist capability
Does not claim independent design critique or block useful checks
